summary: This EOB shows a chemotherapy infusion service where your out-of-pocket costs have exceeded your plan's yearly maximum. You should owe $0 for this claim because the plan's $6,500 out-of-pocket cap has been reached. However, the EOB is asking you to pay $350 in coinsurance. This is a billing error that needs correction.

lines.explanation: This line shows a $350 coinsurance charge (CODE-PR-2: "PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met"). However, your out-of-pocket costs for the year already totaled $6,300 before this claim. Adding the $350 coinsurance would bring your total to $6,650, which exceeds your plan's $6,500 yearly out-of-pocket maximum. Once you hit the maximum, the plan pays 100% of covered charges. The $350 over the cap ($6,650 − $6,500 = $150 minimum) should be the plan's responsibility, not yours. You should not owe any coinsurance on this service.

citations.quote: PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met

math_findings.detail: Your running out-of-pocket total ($6,650.00, including $6,300.00 already used this year) exceeds the plan's $6,500.00 out-of-pocket maximum. Amounts above the maximum are the plan's responsibility, not yours.

actions: Contact Sunrise Health PPO to report that coinsurance was charged after your $6,500 out-of-pocket maximum was exceeded.
Request a corrected EOB showing $0 patient responsibility for line L1, since the plan should cover 100% once the out-of-pocket max is reached.
Do not pay the $350 coinsurance charge until the plan confirms the correction in writing.
escalate_reason: Out-of-pocket maximum overage detected: member was charged $350 coinsurance when their year-to-date out-of-pocket ($6,300) plus this charge ($350) = $6,650, exceeding the $6,500 plan maximum. At least $150 of this charge is the plan's responsibility. Human review required to correct the EOB and issue a refund if member has already paid.
